extracted.intended_audience: authors, researchers, institutional press officers, and journalists
extracted.subtask_description: Press-release and embargo rules for Nature Portfolio journal submissions and accepted papers, covering when and how authors and journalists may communicate about work, press-release distribution, embargo enforcement, and guidance on preprints and conference presentations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authors discouraged from direct solicitation of media
rubrics_metrics.description: We strongly discourage authors and potential authors from direct solicitation of media coverage of material they have submitted to Nature and the Nature Portfolio journals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should avoid contacting media to promote submitted material; the policy aims to prevent premature publicity and preserve the integrity of editorial handling. See also rules on when accepted contributions may be discussed with media (only after publication date confirmed and under embargo).

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for discussing accepted contributions with media
rubrics_metrics.description: Accepted contributions can be discussed with the media only once the publication date has been confirmed and no more than a week before the publication date under our embargo conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors may talk to media about accepted papers in the narrow window (up to one week before publication) and only under the journal's embargo; any publicity outside this timing risks violating policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press-release distribution to registered journalists
rubrics_metrics.description: We produce and distribute press releases summarizing upcoming content to a list of registered journalists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Press releases summarize upcoming journal content; journalists on the distribution list are encouraged to read full papers and are given corresponding authors' names and contact details. Press offices coordinate with editors on content and timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advance access for journalists to full text
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists ... receive access to the full text of papers about a week before publication on a password-protected website, together with other relevant material (for example, an accompanying News and Views article, and any extra images provided by the authors).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advance access is provided via a secure site roughly one week prior to publication to enable informed coverage; journalists are expected to respect the embargo on that material until the stated time and date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embargo requirement and timing clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: The content of the press release and papers is embargoed until the time and date clearly stated on the press release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All recipients must not publish or broadcast details from embargoed materials before the stated embargo lift; the press release explicitly states the embargo time/date to avoid ambiguity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Highlighting especially newsworthy papers
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers that are deemed especially newsworthy are highlighted by a brief summary on the press release for that journal, written by the editors and the press office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors and the press office may add summaries for particularly newsworthy content; this can prompt media contact with authors during the embargo window.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authors should cooperate with journalists contacted during embargo
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors may therefore receive calls or emails from the media during this time; we encourage them to cooperate with journalists so that media coverage of their work is accurate and balanced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When contacted under embargo, authors are encouraged to help ensure accurate reporting, while continuing to respect confidentiality of the peer-review/editorial process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authors may arrange own publicity but must adhere to embargo
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors whose papers are scheduled for publication may also arrange their own publicity (for instance through their institutional press offices), but they must strictly adhere to our media embargo and are advised to coordinate their own publicity with our press office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions and authors can run their own publicity campaigns provided they do not breach the embargo and ideally coordinate timing/content with the journal's press office to avoid conflicts or premature release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose and justification for embargoes
rubrics_metrics.description: Our policy is to release information about our content in a way that provides fair and equal access to the media, allowing it to provide informed comment based on the complete and final version of the paper that is to be published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Embargoes are intended to give journalists equal access and time to obtain independent reactions and report based on the final peer-reviewed article. Premature release 'denies journalists that confidence' and removes their ability to obtain informed reactions from independent researchers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanctions for breaking embargoes
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists who break our embargoes have been removed from the press-release circulation list, and we shall continue to use this sanction when appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Breach of embargo may result in removal from future press-release distributions and other sanctions at the journal's discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preprints and conference presentations are not prior publication
rubrics_metrics.description: We support open communications between researchers whether on a recognised community preprint server or preprint commenting platforms, through discussions at research meetings or online collaborative sites such as wikis or the author's blog. Neither conference presentations nor posting on recognized preprint servers constitute prior publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors may post drafts on established preprint servers before or during submission without preempting journal submission; the journal encourages preprint sharing and provides references to related editorial policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance for researchers responding to media about preprints/conference presentations
rubrics_metrics.description: Researchers may respond to requests from the media in response to a preprint or conference presentation, by providing explanation or clarification of the work, or information about its context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such media responses will not hinder editorial handling, but researchers should be aware that preprint coverage may reduce or pre-empt later coverage. Researchers are advised to make clear that the work 'has not yet undergone peer review, that the findings are provisional and that the conclusions may change.' Authors are also expected to keep the details of the peer review and editorial process confidential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation to reporters covering preprints
rubrics_metrics.description: We also recommend that reporters who cover preprints clearly indicate that the study has not been peer reviewed and that the claims may change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporters should label preprint coverage as provisional and note the lack of peer review to avoid misleading the public about the maturity of the findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journalists encouraged to read full papers and contact authors
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists are encouraged to read the full version of any papers they wish to cover, and are given the names and contact details of corresponding authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The journal expects journalists to consult the full article and, if needed, contact corresponding authors for clarification to support accurate reporting.
